To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a cascade of damage occurs in mutant SOD ALS that initiates in motor neurons and spreads to glia.
a cascade of mutant-dependent, cell type-selective changes occurs in the motor neuron and glial cells that are affected in ALS.
a combination of ribosome profiling and high-throughput RNA sequencing identified a cascade of cell type-specific changes in motor neurons and glial cells in mutant SOD-mediated ALS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of motor neuron disease. In particular
the molecular mechanisms of neurodegenerative disease.
the molecular mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ALS is a neurodegenerative disorder with a cascade of damage initiating in motor neuron and propagating to other cell types.
this work provides a new and detailed understanding of how ALS develops.
the ALS-causing mutations in SOD1 cause disease in a noncell-autonomous fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the disease process begins in motor neurons with a combination of ER stress and synapse dysfunction, and then spreads to glial cells.
the disease is not initiated by a single mechanism, but is the consequence of a cascade of cell type-specific damage.
the initial damage is restricted to the motor neurons and includes synaptic and metabolic abnormalities, ER stress, and selective PERK activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell type-specific damage that we have described in this paper is likely to be a general feature of ALS pathogenesis.

ALS pathogenesis is a cascade of cell type–specific events that begin in motor neurons, which are selectively susceptible to mutant SOD1 toxicity, and that the subsequent spread of disease to astrocytes and oligodendroglia involves cell type–specific changes in gene expression.
ALS is not just a motor neuron disease but a disease that affects multiple cell types in the nervous system.
